focus: Pretérito indefinido: regular endings and key irregulars
focus_note: The pretérito indefinido describes finished actions at a specific time in the past. Regular -ar verbs take -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron; -er/-ir verbs take -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. 'Ir' and 'ser' share the same irregular forms: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. Example: 'Ayer visité la catedral' (Yesterday I visited the cathedral).

lessons.title: Talking about yesterday
lessons.body: For finished actions at a specific time (ayer, anoche, la semana pasada), Spanish uses the pretérito indefinido. Regular -ar verbs end in -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron: cené, cenaste, cenó. Regular -er and -ir verbs end in -í, -iste, -ió: comí, viví. Mind the accent: 'cené' is past, 'cene' is a different form.
lessons.example_translation: Last night I had dinner in the square.

lessons.title: Ir and tener: two irregulars
lessons.body: Some everyday verbs are irregular. 'Ir' (to go) and 'ser' (to be) share the same past forms: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. 'Tener' (to have) changes its stem to tuv-: tuve, tuviste, tuvo, tuvimos. Unlike the regular forms, these irregular ones carry no written accent.
lessons.example: Ayer fuimos al museo y tuvimos suerte.
lessons.example_translation: Yesterday we went to the museum and got lucky.
